frequency_question: How often does administrative and legal friction successfully block the Department of Education from completing a revocation of accrediting authority within a defined administrative window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal departmental action initiated to strip, terminate, or deny renewal of institutional or professional accrediting agency recognition under the Higher Education Act. Excluded are routine renewals or voluntary relinquishments.

cases.name: American Bar Association review of 1996 (Department review of ABA legal education accreditation)
ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) termination proceeding 2016-2018

coverage_note: 3 major contested agency recognition revocation battles identified in modern administrative history; 2 resulted in survival or protracted procedural delay/reinstatement avenues.
known_gaps: Lower-level advisory committee recommendations that did not reach full formal departmental Secretary revocation orders are excluded.
skeleton: Total formal revocation/termination attempts initiated by the Department of Education against recognized accreditors since 1995, divided by those that successfully completed revocation overcoming procedural/legal friction within the target timeframe.
multiplier: 1 successful revocation (ACICS 2022) out of 3 major contested termination/review cycles = 33% success rate for revocation, meaning structural friction successfully prevents revocation in 67% of attempted or contested trajectories.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act and Higher Education Act statutory frameworks governing agency recognition reviews remain stable across multiple presidential administrations.
